title: Defining a new distribution
text: Laplace (double-exponential) density f(y;μ,b)=12bexp⁡(−|y−μ|b)f(y;\mu,b)=\frac{1}{2b}\exp\!\left(-\frac{|y-\mu|}{b}\right), μ∈ℝ\mu\\mathbb{R} b>0b>0. Base R dlaplace, genuinely new distribution. Step 1 — class. continuous, inherit continuous_distrib: Step 2 — density. method distrib_pdf. signature always (distrib, y, theta, log = FALSE), theta named list parameters (element scalar vector aligned y): Two conventions matter. theta indexed positionally (theta[[1]], theta[[2]]) parameter names stay free, log branch always implemented, numerical machinery evaluates density log scale stability. Step 3 — constructor. plain function returning object class metadata filled : params_bounds used fallbacks (finite-difference steps shrunk never step outside parameter’s domain) generate_random_theta(). link_params used downstream modelling code; identity_link() log_link() come linkfunctions7. entire definition. Everything now works: can check fallbacks known closed forms Laplace: object also prints plots like built-distribution:
code: Laplace <- S7::new_class("Laplace", parent = continuous_distrib) S7::method(distrib_pdf, Laplace) <- function(distrib, y, theta, log = FALSE) {   mu <- theta[[1]]   b  <- theta[[2]]   log_d <- -log(2 * b) - abs(y - mu) / b   if (log) log_d else exp(log_d) } laplace_distrib <- function(link_mu = linkfunctions7::identity_link(),                             link_b  = linkfunctions7::log_link()) {   Laplace(     distrib_name = "laplace",     dimension    = "univariate",     bounds       = c(-Inf, Inf),                 # support of Y     params       = c("mu", "b"),     params_interpretation = c(mu = "location", b = "scale"),     n_params     = 2,     params_bounds = list(mu = c(-Inf, Inf), b = c(0, Inf)),     link_params   = list(mu = link_mu, b = link_b)   ) } d  <- laplace_distrib() th <- list(mu = 1, b = 2)  # density (what we defined) distrib_pdf(d, c(0, 1, 3), th) #> [1] 0.15163266 0.25000000 0.09196986  # CDF, quantile, RNG --- all numerical fallbacks distrib_cdf(d, c(-1, 1, 4), th) #> [1] 0.1839397 0.5000000 0.8884349 distrib_quantile(d, c(0.25, 0.5, 0.75), th)   # median is exactly mu = 1 #> [1] -0.3862944  1.0000000  2.3862944 head(distrib_rng(d, 5, th)) #> [1]  5.723932 -2.857153  0.855691  2.715865  0.144959  # score and Hessian --- finite differences of the log-density str(distrib_gradient(d, c(-1, 3), th)) #> List of 2 #>  $ mu: num [1:2] -0.5 0.5 #>  $ b : num [1:2] 1.83e-11 1.83e-11 str(distrib_hessian(d, c(-1, 3), th)) #> List of 3 #>  $ mu_mu: num [1:2] 0 0 #>  $ b_b  : num [1:2] -0.25 -0.25 #>  $ mu_b : num [1:2] 0.25 -0.25  # moments --- numerical integration against the density c(mean = mean(d, th), variance = variance(d, th))  # Laplace variance is 2 b^2 = 8 #>     mean variance  #>        1        8 # analytical Laplace CDF lap_cdf <- function(q, mu, b) {   ifelse(q < mu, 0.5 * exp((q - mu) / b), 1 - 0.5 * exp(-(q - mu) / b)) } q <- c(-3, -1, 0, 1, 4) max(abs(distrib_cdf(d, q, th) - lap_cdf(q, 1, 2)))   # ~1e-10 #> [1] 9.042589e-11 # variance should be exactly 2 b^2 all.equal(variance(d, th), 2 * th$b^2) #> [1] TRUE d #> Distribution: Laplace #> Type:         Continuous #> Dimensions:   univariate #>  #> Parameters: #>   mu (location)           | Link: identity   | Domain: (-Inf, Inf) #>   b  (scale)              | Link: log        | Domain: (0, Inf) plot(d, th)

title: Defining a new distribution
text: discrete distribution, inherit discrete_distrib instead let distrib_pdf probability mass function. one extra requirement support finite lower bound (bounds[1]), every standard count distribution satisfies. discrete fallbacks build cumulative-mass table lower bound, growing geometrically needed.
code: # A shifted-geometric example: P(Y = k) = (1-p) p^k for k = 0, 1, 2, ... Geom <- S7::new_class("Geom", parent = discrete_distrib) S7::method(distrib_pdf, Geom) <- function(distrib, y, theta, log = FALSE) {   p <- theta[[1]]   log_d <- log(1 - p) + y * log(p)   if (log) log_d else exp(log_d) } geom_distrib <- function(link_p = linkfunctions7::logit_link()) {   Geom(     distrib_name = "geometric", dimension = "univariate", bounds = c(0, Inf),     params = "p", params_interpretation = c(p = "success prob."),     n_params = 1, params_bounds = list(p = c(0, 1)),     link_params = list(p = link_p)   ) }  g <- geom_distrib() distrib_cdf(g, 0:3, list(p = 0.6))                      # 1 - p^(k+1) #> [1] 0.4000 0.6400 0.7840 0.8704 distrib_quantile(g, c(0.5, 0.9), list(p = 0.6)) #> [1] 1 4 c(mean = mean(g, list(p = 0.6)))                        # p / (1 - p) = 1.5 #> mean  #>  1.5

text: numerical fallbacks convenient slower less precise analytical formulas. Whenever closed form available, registering method makes take automatically, existing code keeps working. need override everything: subset methods can supplied. Laplace, available closed form. instance CDF, quantile score: Note signature derivative method: must mirror generic, carries scale argument (...). method always returns parameter-scale derivatives; chain rule never implemented hand. generic applies link-scale transformation afterwards caller asks scale = "link". applies distrib_hessian, distrib_expected_hessian, distrib_deriv3 distrib_deriv4; probability-function methods (distrib_pdf, distrib_cdf, distrib_quantile, distrib_rng) keep plain signatures. results identical fallbacks produced, faster exact: practical suggestion order add closed forms: distrib_gradient — single biggest speed-model fitting, since score evaluated every optimisation step. Writing C++ (via Rcpp), built-distributions , helps . distrib_hessian — Newton-type optimisation standard errors. distrib_cdf / distrib_quantile / distrib_rng — fast high-volume simulation tail probabilities. distrib_expected_hessian analytical moments — closed form exists fitting method Fisher scoring, exact moments needed.
code: S7::method(distrib_cdf, Laplace) <- function(distrib, q, theta,                                              lower.tail = TRUE, log.p = FALSE) {   mu <- theta[[1]]; b <- theta[[2]]   res <- ifelse(q < mu, 0.5 * exp((q - mu) / b), 1 - 0.5 * exp(-(q - mu) / b))   if (!lower.tail) res <- 1 - res   if (log.p) log(res) else res }  S7::method(distrib_quantile, Laplace) <- function(distrib, p, theta,                                                   lower.tail = TRUE, log.p = FALSE) {   mu <- theta[[1]]; b <- theta[[2]]   if (log.p) p <- exp(p)   if (!lower.tail) p <- 1 - p   mu - b * sign(p - 0.5) * log(1 - 2 * abs(p - 0.5)) }  # score: d/dmu = sign(y - mu) / b,  d/db = (|y - mu| / b - 1) / b S7::method(distrib_gradient, Laplace) <- function(distrib, y, theta,                                                   scale = c("parameter", "link"), ...) {   mu <- theta[[1]]; b <- theta[[2]]   list(     mu = sign(y - mu) / b,     b  = (abs(y - mu) / b - 1) / b   ) } max(abs(distrib_cdf(d, q, th) - lap_cdf(q, 1, 2)))       # now exact #> [1] 0 str(distrib_gradient(d, c(-1, 3), th))                   # now analytical #> List of 2 #>  $ mu: num [1:2] -0.5 0.5 #>  $ b : num [1:2] 0 0

code: MyLaplace <- S7::new_class("MyLaplace", parent = continuous_distrib)  S7::method(distrib_pdf, MyLaplace) <- function(distrib, y, theta, log = FALSE) {   ld <- -log(2 * theta$b) - abs(y - theta$mu) / theta$b   if (log) ld else exp(ld) }  d2 <- MyLaplace(   distrib_name = "my laplace", dimension = "univariate", bounds = c(-Inf, Inf),   params = c("mu", "b"), params_interpretation = c(mu = "location", b = "scale"),   n_params = 2, params_bounds = list(mu = c(-Inf, Inf), b = c(0, Inf)),   link_params = list(     mu = linkfunctions7::identity_link(),     b  = linkfunctions7::log_link()   ) )  # never implemented, yet available distrib_cdf(d2, 1, list(mu = 0, b = 2)) #> [1] 0.6967347 distrib_gradient(d2, 1, list(mu = 0, b = 2)) #> $mu #> [1] 0.5 #>  #> $b #> [1] -0.25

title: Bernoulli Distribution Object — bernoulli_distrib
text: Bernoulli distribution models binary outcome \(y \\{0, 1\}\) success probability \(\mu\). Probability mass function: $$P(Y=y; \mu) = \mu^y (1-\mu)^{1-y}, \quad y \\{0, 1\}$$ Cumulative distribution function: $$F(q; \mu) = \begin{cases} 0 & q < 0 \\ 1-\mu & 0 \le q < 1 \\ 1 & q \ge 1 \end{cases}$$ Quantile function (generalized inverse): $$Q(p; \mu) = \begin{cases} 0 & p \le 1-\mu \\ 1 & p > 1-\mu \end{cases}$$ Score, observed expected Hessian: $$\dfrac{\partial \ell}{\partial \mu} = \dfrac{y - \mu}{\mu(1-\mu)}, \qquad       \dfrac{\partial^2 \ell}{\partial \mu^2} = -\dfrac{y}{\mu^2} - \dfrac{1-y}{(1-\mu)^2}, \qquad       \mathbb{E}\left[\dfrac{\partial^2 \ell}{\partial \mu^2}\right] = -\dfrac{1}{\mu(1-\mu)}$$ Moments: mean \(\mu\), variance \(\mu(1-\mu)\), skewness \((1-2\mu)/\sqrt{\mu(1-\mu)}\), excess kurtosis \((1 - 6\mu(1-\mu))/(\mu(1-\mu))\). Parameter domains: \(\mu \(0, 1)\) Analytical third- fourth-order derivatives (distrib_deriv3, distrib_deriv4) also available.

title: Beta Distribution Object (Mean-Precision Parameterization) — beta_distrib
text: Beta distribution given mean/precision parameterization: \(\mu\) mean \(\phi\) precision parameter. standard shapes $$\alpha = \mu\phi, \qquad \beta = (1-\mu)\phi$$ Probability density function: $$f(y; \mu, \phi) = \dfrac{\Gamma(\phi)}{\Gamma(\alpha)\Gamma(\beta)}\, y^{\alpha-1} (1-y)^{\beta-1}, \quad 0 < y < 1$$ Cumulative distribution function (\(I_q\) regularized incomplete beta function): $$F(q; \mu, \phi) = I_q(\alpha, \beta)$$ Quantile function: closed form; numerical inverse CDF. Score (\(\psi\) digamma function): $$\dfrac{\partial \ell}{\partial \mu} = \phi\left[\log\left(\dfrac{y}{1-y}\right) - \psi(\alpha) + \psi(\beta)\right]$$ $$\dfrac{\partial \ell}{\partial \phi} = \psi(\phi) - \mu\psi(\alpha) - (1-\mu)\psi(\beta) + \mu\log y + (1-\mu)\log(1-y)$$ Expected Hessian (\(\psi_1\) trigamma function; observed expected Hessians coincide, depend \(y\)): $$\dfrac{\partial^2 \ell}{\partial \mu^2} = -\phi^2\left[\psi_1(\alpha) + \psi_1(\beta)\right], \qquad       \dfrac{\partial^2 \ell}{\partial \mu\,\partial \phi} = -\phi\left[\mu\psi_1(\alpha) - (1-\mu)\psi_1(\beta)\right]$$ $$\dfrac{\partial^2 \ell}{\partial \phi^2} = \psi_1(\phi) - \mu^2\psi_1(\alpha) - (1-\mu)^2\psi_1(\beta)$$ Moments: mean \(\mu\), variance \(\mu(1-\mu)/(\phi+1)\), skewness \(\dfrac{2(1-2\mu)\sqrt{\phi+1}}{(\phi+2)\sqrt{\mu(1-\mu)}}\). Parameter domains: \(\mu \(0, 1)\) \(\phi \(0, +\infty)\) Analytical third- fourth-order derivatives (distrib_deriv3, distrib_deriv4) response derivatives (distrib_grad_y, distrib_hess_y) also available.

title: Binomial Distribution Object — binomial_distrib
text: Binomial distribution models number successes \(n\) independent trials, success probability \(\mu\). number trials \(n\) fixed constructor (size) treated known. Probability mass function: $$P(Y=y; \mu, n) = \dbinom{n}{y} \mu^y (1-\mu)^{n-y}, \quad y \\{0, 1, \dots, n\}$$ Cumulative distribution function: $$F(q; \mu, n) = \sum_{k=0}^{\lfloor q \rfloor} \dbinom{n}{k} \mu^k (1-\mu)^{n-k}$$ Quantile function: generalized inverse \(Q(p) = \min\{y : F(y) \ge p\}\). Score, observed expected Hessian (respect \(\mu\)): $$\dfrac{\partial \ell}{\partial \mu} = \dfrac{y - n\mu}{\mu(1-\mu)}, \qquad       \dfrac{\partial^2 \ell}{\partial \mu^2} = -\dfrac{y}{\mu^2} - \dfrac{n-y}{(1-\mu)^2}, \qquad       \mathbb{E}\left[\dfrac{\partial^2 \ell}{\partial \mu^2}\right] = -\dfrac{n}{\mu(1-\mu)}$$ Moments: mean \(n\mu\), variance \(n\mu(1-\mu)\), skewness \((1-2\mu)/\sqrt{n\mu(1-\mu)}\), excess kurtosis \((1 - 6\mu(1-\mu))/(n\mu(1-\mu))\). Parameter domains: \(\mu \(0, 1)\) \(n \\mathbb{Z}^+\) (fixed constructor, may vary per observation) Analytical third- fourth-order derivatives (distrib_deriv3, distrib_deriv4) also available.

title: Cauchy Distribution Object — cauchy_distrib
text: Cauchy distribution heavy-tailed location-scale distribution location \(\mu\) scale \(\sigma\). moments (mean, variance, higher) undefined. Probability density function: $$f(y; \mu, \sigma) = \dfrac{1}{\pi \sigma \left[1 + \left(\dfrac{y-\mu}{\sigma}\right)^2\right]}$$ Cumulative distribution function: $$F(q; \mu, \sigma) = \dfrac{1}{2} + \dfrac{1}{\pi}\arctan\left(\dfrac{q-\mu}{\sigma}\right)$$ Quantile function: $$Q(p; \mu, \sigma) = \mu + \sigma \tan\left(\pi\left(p - \tfrac{1}{2}\right)\right)$$ Score (\(d = \sigma^2 + (y-\mu)^2\)): $$\dfrac{\partial \ell}{\partial \mu} = \dfrac{2(y-\mu)}{d}, \qquad       \dfrac{\partial \ell}{\partial \sigma} = \dfrac{(y-\mu)^2 - \sigma^2}{\sigma d}$$ Observed Hessian: $$\dfrac{\partial^2 \ell}{\partial \mu^2} = \dfrac{2(y-\mu)^2 - 2\sigma^2}{d^2}, \quad       \dfrac{\partial^2 \ell}{\partial \sigma^2} = \dfrac{\sigma^4 - 4\sigma^2 (y-\mu)^2 - (y-\mu)^4}{\sigma^2 d^2}, \quad       \dfrac{\partial^2 \ell}{\partial \mu\,\partial \sigma} = -\dfrac{4\sigma(y-\mu)}{d^2}$$ Expected Hessian: $$\mathbb{E}\left[\dfrac{\partial^2 \ell}{\partial \mu^2}\right] =       \mathbb{E}\left[\dfrac{\partial^2 \ell}{\partial \sigma^2}\right] = -\dfrac{1}{2\sigma^2}, \qquad       \mathbb{E}\left[\dfrac{\partial^2 \ell}{\partial \mu\,\partial \sigma}\right] = 0$$ Parameter domains: \(\mu \(-\infty, +\infty)\) \(\sigma \(0, +\infty)\) Analytical third- fourth-order derivatives (distrib_deriv3, distrib_deriv4) response derivatives (distrib_grad_y, distrib_hess_y) also available.

text: Closed-form observed third-order derivatives Logistic log-density. Writing \(z = (y-\mu)/\sigma\), \(t = 1/(1+e^{-z})\) \(u = 1-t\), log-density \(\ell = -\log\sigma + g(z)\) \(g(z) = -z - 2\log(1+e^{-z})\), whose derivatives \(z\) $$g_1 = 1-2t, \quad g_2 = -2tu, \quad g_3 = -2tu(1-2t), \quad g_4 = -2tu(1-6tu).$$ Since \(z\) depends parameters, component polynomial \(z\) \(g_j\) coefficients: $$\dfrac{\partial^3 \ell}{\partial \mu^3} = -\dfrac{g_3}{\sigma^3}$$ $$\dfrac{\partial^3 \ell}{\partial \mu^2 \partial \sigma} = -\dfrac{2g_2 + z g_3}{\sigma^3}$$ $$\dfrac{\partial^3 \ell}{\partial \mu \partial \sigma^2} = -\dfrac{2g_1 + 4z g_2 + z^2 g_3}{\sigma^3}$$ $$\dfrac{\partial^3 \ell}{\partial \sigma^3} = -\dfrac{2 + 6z g_1 + 6z^2 g_2 + z^3 g_3}{\sigma^3}$$ expected third derivatives available closed form, expected = TRUE routed expected_derivative_methods.

title: Gumbel Analytical Expected Hessian — distrib_expected_hessian.GumbelDistrib
text: Closed form. model \(w = e^{-Z}\) standard exponential, every expectation needed derivative \(\Gamma\) 2: \(E[w] = 1\), \(E[w \log w] = 1 - \gamma\) \(E[w(\log w)^2] = (1-\gamma)^2 + \pi^2/6 - 1\), together \(E[Z] = \gamma\). Hence $$E\left[\dfrac{\partial^2 \ell}{\partial \mu^2}\right]         = -\dfrac{1}{\sigma^2},       \qquad       E\left[\dfrac{\partial^2 \ell}{\partial \mu \, \partial \sigma}\right]         = \dfrac{1 - \gamma}{\sigma^2},$$ $$E\left[\dfrac{\partial^2 \ell}{\partial \sigma^2}\right]         = -\dfrac{(1-\gamma)^2 + \pi^2/6}{\sigma^2},$$ \(\gamma\) Euler-Mascheroni constant. closed form exists, approx argument ignored.

title: Weibull Analytical Expected Hessian — distrib_expected_hessian.WeibullDistrib
text: Closed form. model \(u = (Y/\mu)^{\sigma}\) standard exponential whatever parameters , every expectation needed derivative \(\Gamma\) 2: \(E[u] = 1\), \(E[u\log u] = 1 - \gamma\) \(E[u(\log u)^2] = (1-\gamma)^2 + \pi^2/6 - 1\). Hence $$E\left[\dfrac{\partial^2 \ell}{\partial \mu^2}\right]         = -\dfrac{\sigma^2}{\mu^2},       \qquad       E\left[\dfrac{\partial^2 \ell}{\partial \sigma^2}\right]         = -\dfrac{1}{\sigma^2}\left\{(1-\gamma)^2 + \dfrac{\pi^2}{6}\right\},$$ $$E\left[\dfrac{\partial^2 \ell}{\partial \mu \, \partial \sigma}\right]         = \dfrac{1 - \gamma}{\mu},$$ \(\gamma\) Euler-Mascheroni constant. closed form exists, approx argument ignored.

Specifically, \(\partial^2 \ell/\partial \phi^2 < 0\) \(\phi < 2(y-\mu)^2/(\mu^2 y)\). condition may violated observations far mean dispersion parameter large, potentially causing numerical instability optimization algorithms rely observed Hessian (e.g., Newton-Raphson). cases, using expected Hessian (distrib_expected_hessian) recommended stable convergence.

title: Gamma Distribution Object (Mean-Variance Parameterization) — gamma_distrib
text: Gamma distribution given mean/variance parameterization: \(\mu\) mean \(\sigma^2\) variance. standard shape \(\alpha\) rate \(\lambda\) recovered $$\alpha = \dfrac{\mu^2}{\sigma^2}, \qquad \lambda = \dfrac{\mu}{\sigma^2}$$ Probability density function: $$f(y; \mu, \sigma^2) = \dfrac{\lambda^\alpha}{\Gamma(\alpha)}\, y^{\alpha-1} e^{-\lambda y}, \quad y > 0$$ Cumulative distribution function (\(\gamma\) lower incomplete gamma function): $$F(q; \mu, \sigma^2) = \dfrac{\gamma(\alpha, \lambda q)}{\Gamma(\alpha)}$$ Quantile function: closed form; numerical inverse CDF. Score (\(\psi\) digamma function): $$\dfrac{\partial \ell}{\partial \mu} = \dfrac{-2\mu\psi(\alpha) + 2\mu\log\lambda + \mu + 2\mu\log y - y}{\sigma^2}$$ $$\dfrac{\partial \ell}{\partial \sigma^2} = -\dfrac{\mu\left[-\mu\psi(\alpha) + \mu + \mu(\log\lambda + \log y) - y\right]}{(\sigma^2)^2}$$ Expected Hessian (\(\psi_1\) trigamma function): $$\mathbb{E}\left[\dfrac{\partial^2 \ell}{\partial \mu^2}\right] = \dfrac{3\sigma^2 - 4\mu^2\psi_1(\alpha)}{(\sigma^2)^2}, \qquad       \mathbb{E}\left[\dfrac{\partial^2 \ell}{\partial \mu\,\partial \sigma^2}\right] = \dfrac{2\mu(\mu^2\psi_1(\alpha) - \sigma^2)}{(\sigma^2)^3}$$ $$\mathbb{E}\left[\dfrac{\partial^2 \ell}{\partial (\sigma^2)^2}\right] = -\dfrac{\mu^2(\mu^2\psi_1(\alpha) - \sigma^2)}{(\sigma^2)^4}$$ observed Hessian available via distrib_hessian.GammaDistrib. Moments: mean \(\mu\), variance \(\sigma^2\), skewness \(2\sqrt{\sigma^2}/\mu\), excess kurtosis \(6\sigma^2/\mu^2\). Parameter domains: \(\mu \(0, +\infty)\) \(\sigma^2 \(0, +\infty)\) Analytical third- fourth-order derivatives (distrib_deriv3, distrib_deriv4) response derivatives (distrib_grad_y, distrib_hess_y) also available.

title: Gaussian Distribution Object (Standard Deviation Parameterization) — gaussian_distrib
text: Gaussian (Normal) distribution parameterized mean \(\mu\) standard deviation \(\sigma\). Probability density function: $$f(y; \mu, \sigma) = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}\,\sigma} \exp\left\{-\dfrac{1}{2}\left(\dfrac{y-\mu}{\sigma}\right)^2\right\}$$ Cumulative distribution function (\(\Phi\) standard normal CDF): $$F(q; \mu, \sigma) = \Phi\left(\dfrac{q-\mu}{\sigma}\right)$$ Quantile function: $$Q(p; \mu, \sigma) = \mu + \sigma\,\Phi^{-1}(p)$$ Score (gradient log-density): $$\dfrac{\partial \ell}{\partial \mu} = \dfrac{y - \mu}{\sigma^2}, \qquad       \dfrac{\partial \ell}{\partial \sigma} = \dfrac{(y - \mu)^2 - \sigma^2}{\sigma^3}$$ Observed Hessian: $$\dfrac{\partial^2 \ell}{\partial \mu^2} = -\dfrac{1}{\sigma^2}, \quad       \dfrac{\partial^2 \ell}{\partial \sigma^2} = \dfrac{\sigma^2 - 3(y-\mu)^2}{\sigma^4}, \quad       \dfrac{\partial^2 \ell}{\partial \mu\,\partial \sigma} = -\dfrac{2(y-\mu)}{\sigma^3}$$ Expected Hessian (negative Fisher information): $$\mathbb{E}\left[\dfrac{\partial^2 \ell}{\partial \mu^2}\right] = -\dfrac{1}{\sigma^2}, \quad       \mathbb{E}\left[\dfrac{\partial^2 \ell}{\partial \sigma^2}\right] = -\dfrac{2}{\sigma^2}, \quad       \mathbb{E}\left[\dfrac{\partial^2 \ell}{\partial \mu\,\partial \sigma}\right] = 0$$ Moments: mean \(\mu\), variance \(\sigma^2\), skewness 0, excess kurtosis 0. Parameter domains: \(\mu \(-\infty, +\infty)\) \(\sigma \(0, +\infty)\) Analytical third- fourth-order derivatives (distrib_deriv3, distrib_deriv4) derivatives respect response (distrib_grad_y, distrib_hess_y) also available.

title: Gumbel Distribution Object — gumbel_distrib
text: Gumbel distribution limit law maximum sample light-tailed distribution, used . location-scale family whole real line, skewed right fixed shape: unlike gaussian, skewness kurtosis constants fitted. Probability density function, \(z = (y-\mu)/\sigma\): $$f(y; \mu, \sigma) = \dfrac{1}{\sigma}\exp\left\{-z - e^{-z}\right\}$$ Cumulative distribution function: $$F(q; \mu, \sigma) = \exp\left\{-e^{-z}\right\}$$ Quantile function: $$Q(p; \mu, \sigma) = \mu - \sigma\log(-\log p)$$ Score, \(w = e^{-z}\): $$\dfrac{\partial \ell}{\partial \mu} = \dfrac{1 - w}{\sigma},       \qquad       \dfrac{\partial \ell}{\partial \sigma}         = \dfrac{z(1 - w) - 1}{\sigma}$$ Observed Hessian: $$\dfrac{\partial^2 \ell}{\partial \mu^2} = -\dfrac{w}{\sigma^2}, \quad       \dfrac{\partial^2 \ell}{\partial \mu \, \partial \sigma}         = -\dfrac{1 - w + zw}{\sigma^2}, \quad       \dfrac{\partial^2 \ell}{\partial \sigma^2}         = \dfrac{1 - 2z + 2zw - z^2 w}{\sigma^2}$$ Expected Hessian: see distrib_expected_hessian.GumbelDistrib. Note \(E[\partial^2 \ell / \partial \mu \, \partial \sigma\)] vanish: location scale orthogonal , unlike symmetric location-scale family, density skewed. Moments: mean \(\mu + \gamma\sigma\), variance \(\pi^2\sigma^2/6\), skewness \(12\sqrt{6}\,\zeta(3)/\pi^3 \approx 1.1395\) excess kurtosis \(12/5\), last two free parameters. Relation Weibull. \(Y\) Gumbel \(e^{-Y}\) Weibull, weibull_distrib family log scale reversed; two share expectations produce information matrices. Minima. distribution minima reflection: fit family \(-Y\), use transformation affine_transform(scale = -1). Higher orders. Third fourth derivatives registered closed form come numerical fallbacks (numerical_deriv3, numerical_deriv4). Parameter Domains: \(\mu \(-\infty, +\infty)\) \(\sigma \(0, +\infty)\)

title: Inverse-Gaussian Distribution Object (Mean-Dispersion Parameterization) — invgauss_distrib
text: Inverse-Gaussian distribution given mean/dispersion parameterization, mean \(\mu\) dispersion \(\phi\). Probability density function: $$f(y; \mu, \phi) = \sqrt{\dfrac{1}{2\pi\phi y^3}} \exp\left\{-\dfrac{(y-\mu)^2}{2\phi\mu^2 y}\right\}, \quad y > 0$$ Cumulative distribution function (\(\Phi\) standard normal CDF): $$F(q; \mu, \phi) = \Phi\!\left(\sqrt{\tfrac{1}{\phi q}}\left(\tfrac{q}{\mu}-1\right)\right) + e^{2/(\phi\mu)}\, \Phi\!\left(-\sqrt{\tfrac{1}{\phi q}}\left(\tfrac{q}{\mu}+1\right)\right)$$ Quantile function: closed form; numerical inverse CDF. Score: $$\dfrac{\partial \ell}{\partial \mu} = \dfrac{y - \mu}{\phi\mu^3}, \qquad       \dfrac{\partial \ell}{\partial \phi} = \dfrac{(y - \mu)^2 - y\mu^2\phi}{2y\phi^2\mu^2}$$ Observed Hessian: $$\dfrac{\partial^2 \ell}{\partial \mu^2} = -\dfrac{3y - 2\mu}{\phi\mu^4}, \quad       \dfrac{\partial^2 \ell}{\partial \phi^2} = \dfrac{\phi - 2(y-\mu)^2/(\mu^2 y)}{2\phi^3}, \quad       \dfrac{\partial^2 \ell}{\partial \mu\,\partial \phi} = -\dfrac{y - \mu}{\phi^2\mu^3}$$ Expected Hessian: $$\mathbb{E}\left[\dfrac{\partial^2 \ell}{\partial \mu^2}\right] = -\dfrac{1}{\phi\mu^3}, \quad       \mathbb{E}\left[\dfrac{\partial^2 \ell}{\partial \phi^2}\right] = -\dfrac{1}{2\phi^2}, \quad       \mathbb{E}\left[\dfrac{\partial^2 \ell}{\partial \mu\,\partial \phi}\right] = 0$$ Moments: mean \(\mu\), variance \(\phi\mu^3\), skewness \(3\sqrt{\phi\mu}\), excess kurtosis \(15\phi\mu\). Parameter domains: \(\mu \(0, +\infty)\) \(\phi \(0, +\infty)\) Analytical third- fourth-order derivatives (distrib_deriv3, distrib_deriv4) response derivatives (distrib_grad_y, distrib_hess_y) also available.

title: Laplace Distribution Object — laplace_distrib
text: Laplace (double-exponential) distribution location \(\mu\) scale \(b\). Probability density function: $$f(y; \mu, b) = \dfrac{1}{2b} \exp\left(-\dfrac{|y-\mu|}{b}\right)$$ Cumulative distribution function: $$F(q; \mu, b) = \begin{cases} \tfrac{1}{2}\exp\left(\tfrac{q-\mu}{b}\right) & q < \mu \\ 1 - \tfrac{1}{2}\exp\left(-\tfrac{q-\mu}{b}\right) & q \ge \mu \end{cases}$$ Quantile function: $$Q(p; \mu, b) = \mu - b\,\mathrm{sign}(p - \tfrac{1}{2})\,\log\left(1 - 2\left|p - \tfrac{1}{2}\right|\right)$$ Score (defined almost everywhere): $$\dfrac{\partial \ell}{\partial \mu} = \dfrac{\mathrm{sign}(y-\mu)}{b}, \qquad       \dfrac{\partial \ell}{\partial b} = \dfrac{1}{b}\left(\dfrac{|y-\mu|}{b} - 1\right)$$ Observed Hessian: $$\dfrac{\partial^2 \ell}{\partial \mu^2} = 0, \quad       \dfrac{\partial^2 \ell}{\partial \mu\,\partial b} = -\dfrac{\mathrm{sign}(y-\mu)}{b^2}, \quad       \dfrac{\partial^2 \ell}{\partial b^2} = \dfrac{b - 2|y-\mu|}{b^3}$$ Expected Hessian (Fisher information score variance; see ): $$\mathbb{E}\left[\dfrac{\partial^2 \ell}{\partial \mu^2}\right] = -\dfrac{1}{b^2}, \quad       \mathbb{E}\left[\dfrac{\partial^2 \ell}{\partial b^2}\right] = -\dfrac{1}{b^2}, \quad       \mathbb{E}\left[\dfrac{\partial^2 \ell}{\partial \mu\,\partial b}\right] = 0$$ Moments: mean \(\mu\), variance \(2b^2\), skewness 0, excess kurtosis 3. Non-differentiability. density kink \(y = \mu\), log-likelihood differentiable \(\mu\). package marks via params_smooth = c(mu = FALSE, b = TRUE) handles follows: score (distrib_gradient) exists almost everywhere, equal \(\mathrm{sign}(y-\mu)/b\); observed Hessian (distrib_hessian) \(\partial^2 \ell / \partial \mu^2 = 0\), Newton-Raphson update \(\mu\); expected Hessian (distrib_expected_hessian) implemented closed form variance score, giving correct Fisher information \(1/b^2\) \(\mu\) making Fisher scoring appropriate estimation method. closed form exists, approx argument ignored distribution. Parameter Domains: \(\mu \(-\infty, +\infty)\) \(b \(0, +\infty)\)

text: Write \(h_i = g_i^{-1}\), \(\theta_i = h_i(\eta_i)\). parameter carries link, Jacobian \(\partial\theta/\partial\eta\) diagonal multivariate Faa di Bruno formula factorises. derivative whose multi-index involves distinct parameters \(p_1,\dots,p_r\) multiplicities \(m_1,\dots,m_r\), $$\frac{\partial^k \ell}{\partial \eta_{p_1}^{m_1} \cdots \partial \eta_{p_r}^{m_r}}       = \sum_{j_1=1}^{m_1} \cdots \sum_{j_r=1}^{m_r}         \ell_{\,p_1^{j_1} \cdots p_r^{j_r}} \prod_{t=1}^{r} B_{m_t, j_t}\!\left(h_{p_t}', h_{p_t}'', \dots\right)$$ \(\ell_{\cdot}\) parameter-scale derivatives \(B_{m,j}\) partial (incomplete) Bell polynomials. low-order cases $$\frac{\partial \ell}{\partial \eta_a} = \ell_a h', \qquad       \frac{\partial^2 \ell}{\partial \eta_a^2} = \ell_{aa} (h')^2 + \ell_a h''$$ $$\frac{\partial^3 \ell}{\partial \eta_a^3} = \ell_{aaa}(h')^3 + 3\ell_{aa} h' h'' + \ell_a h'''$$ $$\frac{\partial^4 \ell}{\partial \eta_a^4} = \ell_{aaaa}(h')^4 + 6\ell_{aaa}(h')^2 h'' + \ell_{aa}\left(4h'h''' + 3(h'')^2\right) + \ell_a h''''$$ mixed derivatives across different parameters simply multiply corresponding factors (e.g. \(\partial^2\ell/\partial\eta_a\partial\eta_b = \ell_{ab} h_a' h_b'\)). expected Hessian first-order term vanishes score zero expectation, information transforms congruence \(\mathrm{diag}(h')\,\mathbb{E}[H]\,\mathrm{diag}(h')\). inverse-link derivatives \(h', h'', h''', h''''\) obtained linkinvderiv, link-scale derivatives available order 4 every link linkfunctions7.

title: Lognormal Distribution Object (Log-Scale Parameterization) — lognormal_distrib
text: Lognormal distribution describes variable whose logarithm Gaussian mean \(\mu\) variance \(\sigma^2\) (log scale). Write \(r = \log y - \mu\). Probability density function: $$f(y; \mu, \sigma^2) = \dfrac{1}{y\sqrt{2\pi\sigma^2}} \exp\left\{-\dfrac{(\log y - \mu)^2}{2\sigma^2}\right\}, \quad y > 0$$ Cumulative distribution function (\(\Phi\) standard normal CDF): $$F(q; \mu, \sigma^2) = \Phi\left(\dfrac{\log q - \mu}{\sqrt{\sigma^2}}\right)$$ Quantile function: $$Q(p; \mu, \sigma^2) = \exp\left(\mu + \sqrt{\sigma^2}\,\Phi^{-1}(p)\right)$$ Score: $$\dfrac{\partial \ell}{\partial \mu} = \dfrac{r}{\sigma^2}, \qquad       \dfrac{\partial \ell}{\partial \sigma^2} = \dfrac{r^2 - \sigma^2}{2\sigma^4}$$ Observed Hessian: $$\dfrac{\partial^2 \ell}{\partial \mu^2} = -\dfrac{1}{\sigma^2}, \quad       \dfrac{\partial^2 \ell}{\partial (\sigma^2)^2} = \dfrac{1}{2\sigma^4} - \dfrac{r^2}{\sigma^6}, \quad       \dfrac{\partial^2 \ell}{\partial \mu\,\partial \sigma^2} = -\dfrac{r}{\sigma^4}$$ Expected Hessian: $$\mathbb{E}\left[\dfrac{\partial^2 \ell}{\partial \mu^2}\right] = -\dfrac{1}{\sigma^2}, \quad       \mathbb{E}\left[\dfrac{\partial^2 \ell}{\partial (\sigma^2)^2}\right] = -\dfrac{1}{2\sigma^4}, \quad       \mathbb{E}\left[\dfrac{\partial^2 \ell}{\partial \mu\,\partial \sigma^2}\right] = 0$$ Moments: mean \(e^{\mu + \sigma^2/2}\), variance \((e^{\sigma^2}-1)e^{2\mu+\sigma^2}\), skewness \((e^{\sigma^2}+2)\sqrt{e^{\sigma^2}-1}\), excess kurtosis \(e^{4\sigma^2}+2e^{3\sigma^2}+3e^{2\sigma^2}-6\). Parameter domains: \(\mu \(-\infty, +\infty)\) \(\sigma^2 \(0, +\infty)\) Analytical third- fourth-order derivatives (distrib_deriv3, distrib_deriv4) response derivatives (distrib_grad_y, distrib_hess_y) also available.

title: Negative Binomial Distribution Object (NB2) — negbin_distrib
text: Negative Binomial distribution (NB2) given mean/dispersion parameterization, mean \(\mu\) dispersion \(\theta\) (smaller \(\theta\) means overdispersion). Write \(s = \theta + \mu\). Probability mass function: $$P(Y=y; \mu, \theta) = \dfrac{\Gamma(y+\theta)}{y!\,\Gamma(\theta)} \left(\dfrac{\theta}{s}\right)^\theta \left(\dfrac{\mu}{s}\right)^y$$ Cumulative distribution function: $$F(q; \mu, \theta) = \sum_{k=0}^{\lfloor q \rfloor} P(Y=k; \mu, \theta)$$ Quantile function: generalized inverse \(Q(p) = \min\{y \\mathbb{N}_0 : F(y) \ge p\}\). Score (\(\psi\) digamma function): $$\dfrac{\partial \ell}{\partial \mu} = \dfrac{\theta}{s}\left(\dfrac{y}{\mu} - 1\right), \qquad       \dfrac{\partial \ell}{\partial \theta} = \psi(y+\theta) - \psi(\theta) + \log\left(\dfrac{\theta}{s}\right) + \dfrac{\mu - y}{s}$$ Observed Hessian (\(\psi_1\) trigamma function): $$\dfrac{\partial^2 \ell}{\partial \mu^2} = \dfrac{y+\theta}{s^2} - \dfrac{y}{\mu^2}, \qquad       \dfrac{\partial^2 \ell}{\partial \mu\,\partial \theta} = \dfrac{y-\mu}{s^2}$$ $$\dfrac{\partial^2 \ell}{\partial \theta^2} = \psi_1(y+\theta) - \psi_1(\theta) + \dfrac{\mu}{\theta s} + \dfrac{y-\mu}{s^2}$$ Expected Hessian: $$\mathbb{E}\left[\dfrac{\partial^2 \ell}{\partial \mu^2}\right] = -\dfrac{\theta}{\mu s}, \qquad       \mathbb{E}\left[\dfrac{\partial^2 \ell}{\partial \theta^2}\right] = \mathbb{E}[\psi_1(Y+\theta)] - \psi_1(\theta) + \dfrac{\mu}{\theta s}, \qquad       \mathbb{E}\left[\dfrac{\partial^2 \ell}{\partial \mu\,\partial \theta}\right] = 0$$ Moments: mean \(\mu\), variance \(\mu + \mu^2/\theta\), skewness \((\theta + 2\mu)/\sqrt{\mu\theta(\theta+\mu)}\), excess kurtosis \(6/\theta + \theta/(\mu(\theta+\mu))\). Parameter domains: \(\mu \(0, +\infty)\) \(\theta \(0, +\infty)\) Analytical third- fourth-order derivatives (distrib_deriv3, distrib_deriv4) also available.

title: Poisson Distribution Object — poisson_distrib
text: Poisson distribution models counts \(y \\{0, 1, 2, \dots\}\) mean (variance) \(\mu\). Probability mass function: $$P(Y=y; \mu) = \dfrac{\mu^y e^{-\mu}}{y!}$$ Cumulative distribution function: $$F(q; \mu) = \sum_{k=0}^{\lfloor q \rfloor} \dfrac{\mu^k e^{-\mu}}{k!}$$ Quantile function: generalized inverse \(Q(p) = \min\{y \\mathbb{N}_0 : F(y) \ge p\}\). Score, observed expected Hessian: $$\dfrac{\partial \ell}{\partial \mu} = \dfrac{y - \mu}{\mu}, \qquad       \dfrac{\partial^2 \ell}{\partial \mu^2} = -\dfrac{y}{\mu^2}, \qquad       \mathbb{E}\left[\dfrac{\partial^2 \ell}{\partial \mu^2}\right] = -\dfrac{1}{\mu}$$ Moments: mean \(\mu\), variance \(\mu\), skewness \(1/\sqrt{\mu}\), excess kurtosis \(1/\mu\). Parameter domains: \(\mu \(0, +\infty)\) Analytical third- fourth-order derivatives (distrib_deriv3, distrib_deriv4) also available.
